panels.description: Wide, full page width. The fort at Udayagiri under a grey afternoon, rain sweeping in from the west and blurring the line of the hills behind it. A lone rider comes in through the gate: Nagoji on a bay horse, horse and rider dark with wet. No cloak; the white coat is soaked dark at the shoulders. Ananthan Pillai look (CONTINUITY, ch24 onward): white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, buckled European riding boots, silver chain of office, talwar at the hip; bare-headed, NO hat or tricorn, NO turban, Kerala topknot; clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, grey at the temples.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The ola came on a day that smelled of ink and rain.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: By the time I reached the fort, my temper was short.

panels.description: Interior. Ramayyan's small room off the war hall. This panel fixes the floor plan for every interior panel in the chapter: whitewashed laterite walls; Ramayyan sits cross-legged on a low wooden seat against the back wall; behind him is the room's one window, unglazed, with wooden bars, opening on a narrow courtyard where a single neem tree stands in the rain; an oil lamp burns in a niche in the side wall to his right; a low table in front of him, and across it a single low stool facing him, with the door behind the stool. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) has palm-leaf bundles at his knee. Nagoji in the doorway, shaking rain from his coat sleeves, water running off his topknot.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You ride in all weathers now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The marches do not stay still when the sun hides.

panels.description: Medium, over Ramayyan's shoulder. He nods Nagoji toward the stool. On the table between them, a single palm leaf lies weighted with a small river stone. Ramayyan's hands rest on his knees, well away from it.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Sit. We have a matter to discuss that is not for the hall.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table, Nagoji now on the stool, coat dripping onto the floor. Ramayyan's fingers lift the stone.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You have been busy. Putting out small fires along the northern border.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You told me that was my work.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It is. So is this.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji's face, close, lit from the side by the niche lamp, reading. The leaf is in the foreground seen edge-on from behind, so no writing faces the reader. His expression has gone still. Letterer's note: all text from leaves and letters in this chapter is set as CAPTION (letter) or CAPTION (leaf), an italic box with a pale palm-leaf tint, distinct from Nagoji's narration. The art never shows legible script.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not his hand. The curves and strokes were Deccan.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Nagoji Sawant, who rode once under our banners and now rides for a southern king.

panels.description: Medium. Nagoji looking up from the leaf at Ramayyan, who is unhurried.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: From Raghuji Bhonsle's camp.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: From one of his sardars. Carried by a trader who thought he was being clever and by a spy who was cleverer.

panels.description: Wide, a painted world behind the words, cool and dusty. Maratha horsemen under saffron swallow-tailed pennants lead Chanda Sahib away from the walls of Tiruchirappalli, his wrists chained, riders on every side. Distance, not faces.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Brother in arms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Chanda Sahib rots in our chains, but his capture has only sharpened our appetite for the Carnatic.

panels.description: Wide. A Maratha host riding south across open plain toward a far green line of palms and sea. Dust hanging gold behind them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: If you return now, you will have estates confirmed, your family freed from certain levies, your advice heard.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: You could help guide our charge south so that we do not waste men as company fools did at Colachel.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's eyes and brow above the edge of the leaf. The bare laterite wall behind him, lamplight wavering on it, takes the upper half of the frame for the letter boxes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: You also know the weaknesses of this southern kingdom, for all its new walls.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: If you stay, you risk being trapped when the map changes under your feet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: For now, tell us what you know.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Flashback, warm and sun-bleached, the Carnatic after a skirmish, horses blowing behind. Young Nagoji, in his early twenties, NO grey, lean, in a plain cotton angarkha and a dusty saffron turban, talwar at his hip; clean-shaven chin, moustache, gold stud; dusty and grinning. The sardar, on the left, is plainly older: in his forties, thick-bodied and heavy-jowled, a grey-streaked moustache and a clean chin (no beards in this frame), a larger turban with a jewelled turban ornament, a brocade-edged angarkha; his hand is clapped on Nagoji's shoulder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He did not sign his name, but the tone told me who had written it.

copy.speaker: SARDAR
copy.text: You see further than I do, Nagoji. One day that will get you killed or much land.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here he was, offering the latter and implying the former.

panels.description: Nagoji setting the leaf back on the table. Ramayyan regarding him levelly.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And you did not burn it. Interesting.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It is not my place to burn your past. Only to weigh what it asks of your present.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, wary.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You think this is a trick.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Everything is a trick. That does not mean it is not also sincere.

panels.description: Ramayyan leaning back on his seat, hands resting lightly on his knees. The barred window behind him, the neem beyond it bowed with rain.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They ask for information. Not yet for betrayal.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: That comes later, if the first request goes unchallenged.

panels.description: Cutaway, wide, soft-edged like the letter images on page 2. A toll post on the road in from the north, in rain. A trader's pack horse stands with its saddlebags open; a toll clerk in plain cotton, Ramayyan's man, holds a folded palm-leaf ola up out of the wet and turns it to read, while the trader, oblivious, haggles with a second clerk over his cloth bales. No legible script. Both balloons tail off-panel to the room.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: I could have had the letter intercepted and never told you. Instead, I show you. Ask yourself why.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: You want to see what I do. You want to move me from the "risk" column in your books to the "asset" one, one way or the other.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Exterior, from the narrow courtyard in the storm: rain driving against the laterite wall of Ramayyan's room, water sheeting off the tiled eaves and down the stone, the neem bowed and streaming, the one barred window a small square of lamplight with no figures readable through it. Ramayyan's balloons tail from the window.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Maharaja trusts you more than most of his own nobles. That trust has kept some of this kingdom's bones from breaking.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It also makes you a potential crack.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I prefer to test a wall before the storm does.

panels.description: Wide, warm Deccan light, soft-edged like memory. A village courtyard on the black soil: Nagoji's father, grey and bent, straightening his back; his brother's wife at the hearth ladling ghee; two nephews in new cloth. No inset.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Estates confirmed. Family freed from certain levies. Advice heard.

panels.description: Wide, cold and grey, the same soft edges turned hard. A Travancore star fort, taken: saffron swallow-tailed Maratha pennants flying from its bastions, its cannon swung round to point inland at Travancore villages, Maratha horse pouring past it down from the northern ghats. Offshore, small against the sea, European ships with men watching from the rails.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I could also see the other images the leaf did not paint.

panels.description: Left half of the third tier. Padmini's estate at night: the pepper vines and the jackfruit tree lit by fire, Maratha riders silhouetted against the flames. No bodies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not Kollamkara's men. My own countrymen.

panels.description: Right half of the third tier, side by side with 4.3. Velinadu at dusk: Revathi (deep indigo sari with gold, tali, grey threading her hair, jasmine in her braid, sandalwood line at the hairline) at a window, watching smoke on the horizon.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Velinadu, folded by yet another power into a larger map.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Back in the room, two-shot across the low table: Nagoji with the Deccan leaf flat under his palm; Ramayyan on his seat, precise, a faint dryness at the mouth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They ask for what I know.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If I tell them nothing, I insult men I once rode beside. If I tell them everything, I open this kingdom's ribs.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If you tell them only what helps them avoid company mistakes without helping them cut us, you may keep two houses from collapsing on each other.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Half truths.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Selected truths.

panels.description: Ramayyan leaning forward into the lamplight, eyes sharpened.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: This is the test, Ananthan. Not whether you will ride north tomorrow. I do not believe you will.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, the lamp flame small in his eyes.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: The test is whether, when confronted with a choice between making Travancore easier prey and making your old masters slightly less blind...

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: ...you know where to place your weight.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Ramayyan's thin fingers sliding a blank palm leaf and an iron stylus across the table toward the Deccan leaf.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Write. I will not guide your hand.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I will read what you write. Then I will decide what to send.

panels.description: Tight on both of Nagoji's hands. His right hand closes on the iron stylus the way a swordsman grips a hilt, nails healed but ridged. His left hand holds the blank leaf in the palm-leaf writer's grip, the white cuff slid back to show the old Portuguese brand on the left forearm near the wrist, pale and puckered with age, no letters or numerals.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The stylus felt heavier than any sword.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji bent over the leaf, the stylus moving. Flowing out of the lamplight around him, one bleeding into the next like smoke, four fragments with only one face among them: a woman's hands tying a black thread charm on a young man's wrist (hands only); Padmini, her hair still black, handing a brass cup of water under the jackfruit tree; a thin hand slipping from a rope in a storm-black sea (Keshavrao, hand only, as in Chapter 24 panel 19.1); and, tiny against the sky, a lanky boy on a palm-top platform with a long brass spyglass to his eye (as in Chapter 11 panel 1.2).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not quickly, not slowly.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji writing, stylus scoring the leaf, Ramayyan motionless across the table. Inset, upper corner, sun-hard: Colachel beach. A square of Dutch East India Company infantry in blue coats and black tricorns, muskets levelled, pressed against the waterline on a narrow strip of sand, boots sinking in the wet ground; Travancore Nair infantry and horse closing from both flanks. Plain flags, no lettering or monograms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I wrote of Colachel, but not of every detail.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I wrote of European arrogance, how it made them underestimate Indian infantry.

panels.description: A new star bastion on a Travancore wall, a battery of guns on it, masons patching a section of wall below. The panel is drawn half in lamp-shadow, as if a hand had passed across it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I wrote none of this. Nor the weaknesses we had only marked for later.

panels.description: Drawn in the same light-and-shadow style as 6.2. In the lit half: a Maratha sardar and the Nair chief of a coastal house (topknot, bare chest, white mundu, gold earrings) seated as equals on a tiled verandah, a betel box between them. In the shadowed half, as if a hand had passed across it: Maratha tribute chests, closed, pushed back into the dark.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I wrote that they would need to treat coastal houses as partners, not possessions.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not write what that would cost my old masters.

panels.description: Ramayyan reading the finished leaf in silence, eyes stopped on one line. Nagoji across from him flexing his aching writing hand.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You have given them enough to avoid dying stupidly if they ever fight Europeans on beaches.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You have not given them a clear path through our forts.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji, level, forearms on the table.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If they do come, I would rather they hit Dutch and other company men effectively than stumble into our guns like idiots.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But I will not pave their road over Padmini's fields or Velinadu's shrines.

panels.description: Ramayyan nodding, the read leaf laid back on the table between them, his hands off it.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The messenger waits at the border. He is patient.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if he is not?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then his horse will sink in sand one day and I will not weep.

panels.description: Tight insert. Ramayyan's thin bare wrist and fingers, the edge of his plain white cloth, reaching for the leaf; Nagoji's broader hand, nails ridged, the white coat cuff with its brass button, coming down over his and pinning it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No.

panels.description: Ramayyan looking up, eyebrows raised. Nagoji's hand still covering his.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It is a good letter. It allows me to keep a foot in the north. To answer a friend. To be a Maratha who helps Travancore.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yes.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji. Nothing theatrical. Quiet certainty.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am not a Maratha who helps Travancore.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Not anymore.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji standing at the lamp niche in the side wall with both leaves in his hand, the answer and the Deccan letter, their edges a finger's width from the flame. Ramayyan still seated behind him, turned on his seat to watch.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (soft)
copy.text: Ananthan. Once you do this, there is no echo. You become silent to them.

panels.description: Small inset, top left corner, overlapping 8.2. Tight on Nagoji's profile in the lamplight, eyes on the flame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know.

panels.description: Large, about half the page. The two leaves catching: dry palm cracking and curling, black smoke lifting, the flame bright on both men's faces. Ramayyan now standing too, a pace behind. Hold it.
Narrow strip, about a sixth of the page. Low angle, floor level. Grey ash drifting down onto the stone floor. Nagoji's buckled boots beyond it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have no advice for the Bhonsle's men.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My sword is here. My words stay here.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, a full third of the page so the face reads. Ramayyan watching the last spark die, and smiling. It must read as unlike his earlier thin, dry smiles (Chapter 10 panel 2.1, Chapter 11 panel 20.3, Chapter 12 panel 3.5, Chapter 21 panel 6.5): open, reaching the eyes, a little surprised at itself.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the first time in all the years I had known him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not a baring of teeth.

panels.description: Two-shot, the smoke still hanging between them.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You have closed a door on one future.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You could have written a different letter, one that made this court easier to cut. We would have acted.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You would have cut me before they could cut you.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yes. Today, I do not have to.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Ramayyan's hand and stylus scoring two short lines into a small fresh leaf. Compose it as a deliberate echo of Chapter 1 panel 1.2, the Goa clerk's hand and ledger: same angle, same closeness, a different hand. No legible script on the leaf, only scored marks; the entry is carried by the CAPTION (leaf) box.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (leaf)
copy.text: Sawant, Nagoji: tested with northern letter. Burned the bridge himself. Is ours.

panels.description: Ramayyan holding the small leaf where Nagoji can see it. He does not hide it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You keep this in your records.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I keep it in mine. You keep it in your bones.

panels.description: Ramayyan drawing out an older bundle of leaves, edges worn soft from handling, tied with faded cord.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: There is one more thing. Since you have proven yourself today, you may as well know the shape of other pieces on the board.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Ramayyan, flat, fact-giving, the old bundle in his hands. In the foreground, the back of Nagoji's head and the set of his shoulders.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Portuguese priest. Father Duarte. You confronted him when the embassy arrived.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I remember.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He has been in my pay for eleven years.

panels.description: Small inset, top left, overlapping 10.2. Nagoji's face, struck.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What?

panels.description: Wide flashback, desaturated. The Goa waterfront at night, shipping and warehouse walls. Father Duarte, younger (thin, scholar's stoop, grey eyes, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO collar tab), passing a folded, sealed packet to an unnamed Marakkar trader in the shadow of a warehouse arch. The trader wears a white skullcap and plain coastal cotton, clean-shaven, no scar; he is NOT Ibrahim Marakkar, with no short coat and no vest.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Since before you washed up on this coast.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: A man of conscience, he said. A man who had seen what his empire did to those it conquered and found the taste bitter.

panels.description: Flashback, the interrogation chamber from Chapter 1. Reuse the approved Chapter 1 panel 8.3 frame, desaturated, rather than generating it again: shot from high in the vault, small figures, the stool, the brazier, João's broad back, and Duarte standing just far enough back. If it must be redrawn: João broad and heavy in a brown leather jerkin over a cream shirt, wide belt, iron key ring, NOT a priest, no cassock; Duarte apart in his black cassock; Nagoji on the stool in torn ochre rags; no noose, and any rope hangs from the iron ring. Distance, not detail. No gore.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: He tortured me. He watched while João...

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Yes. He did.

panels.description: Cutaway, present day, not seen through any window: the Travancore drill ground on a dry, bright day, set off with the same soft edges as the other voice-over images. European deserters in white Travancore coats drilling local gunners at a cannon. All balloons off-panel.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: And then he spent years sending us reports on Portuguese troop movements.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The European defectors.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Some of them came because Father Duarte whispered in their ears.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Back in the room. Nagoji alone in the frame, sitting back on the stool, the lamp niche's glow beside him, looking at nothing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Eleven years.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The man who watched my torture had spent eleven years secretly serving the crown I had chosen to die for.

panels.description: Nagoji leaning in, low-voiced. Ramayyan's thin smile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: When he came with the embassy. Did he know...

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: That you had become one of our generals? Of course he knew. I told him myself, years ago.

panels.description: Flashback, Chapter 24: the parade ground by the stables. Duarte, older (grey hair, deeper stoop, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO collar tab), faces Nagoji, who wears his white Travancore coat. Duarte's hand rising toward the cross at his throat and stopping short, as in Chapter 24 panel 16.3.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: He asked to come. Perhaps he wanted to know if you would kill him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Perhaps he wanted to give you the chance.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Was any of it real? The guilt? The hesitation?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: All of it was real. That is why he is useful.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: He serves us because serving us is the only penance he can find.

panels.description: Ramayyan on his seat, the old bundle on his knee, patient as a ledger.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And you let me threaten him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I let you have your moment. You needed it. He needed it. Now you both know where you stand.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Where do we stand?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Exterior, looking in through the barred window from the courtyard: the two men framed small in the lamplit room, Ramayyan's back to us, Nagoji facing the window beyond him, the dripping neem in the foreground.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: On the same side of the wall.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Though you came to it by different doors.

panels.description: Wide flashback, soft-edged: the parade ground in Chapter 24, the moment of Chapter 24 panel 19.3. Duarte (older, grey hair, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO collar tab) nodding slowly; Nagoji in his white coat and topknot seen from behind at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: DUARTE (flashback)
copy.text: Then we are alike in that. More than I would have thought.

panels.description: Back in the room. Close on Nagoji, the niche lamp lighting one side of his face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had not been speaking only of choices and regrets.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had been speaking of service to the same crown.

panels.description: Ramayyan gathering the old leaves and tying the faded cord, not looking up.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: That does not erase what he did. But it may change what it means.

panels.description: Ramayyan at the door, the bundle under his arm, pausing on the threshold and looking back.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: One more thing. The priest has asked to remain. Not as an envoy. Permanently.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: De Lannoy has been asking for a chaplain for years.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Imagined, soft-edged: a small chapel of local stone with a simple wooden cross, a lamp on a plain altar, the chapel of Chapter 28 panel 10.1. De Lannoy (tall, pale hair, white Travancore coat) and Duarte (grey, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO collar tab) kneeling side by side before it. Do not attach the temple-priest sheet to this panel or to any Duarte panel.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: This kingdom collects strange pieces.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: This kingdom uses what it finds. As it used you. As it used me.

panels.description: Wide. The narrow courtyard after the rain, the neem dripping, its leaves gleaming. Padmini Amma (older now, grey in her coiled hair, simple gold, long walking stick) waiting under it as Nagoji steps out of Ramayyan's door.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Ram summoned you. He had the look he gets when balancing pots on a shelf.

panels.description: Two-shot under the neem, Padmini leaning on her stick, Nagoji beside her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He tested a shelf. It did not crack.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Good. I am too old to build new ones for this house.

panels.description: Velinadu, lamplight. Revathi (deep indigo sari with gold, tali, grey threading her hair, jasmine in her braid, sandalwood line at the hairline) seated on a mat by a lamp, a palm leaf held in her left hand, the stylus quick in her right, mouth firm.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi's answer came later, in one of her sharp letters.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: You have chosen to make the Deccan less blind without making Travancore naked.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: That is a narrow path. Do not pretend it is not also a chain.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, the tallest panel on the page. Weeks on: evening on the fort's rampart, the stones dry, the sky clearing. Nagoji standing alone on the wall walk, small against the sky, looking north, where a new bank of cloud is building over the hills.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She was right. Every choice binds.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had chosen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The entry had been made. The storm that would test those lines had not yet arrived.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: But when it did, at least I would not have to wonder whose side of the wall I was standing on.

layout.policy: compositor assigns rows from panel counts

Wide, full page width. The fort at Udayagiri under a grey afternoon, rain sweeping in from the west and blurring the line of the hills behind it. A lone rider comes in through the gate: Nagoji on a bay horse, horse and rider dark with wet. No cloak; the white coat is soaked dark at the shoulders.
